name: Fontodi Flaccianello della Pieve Colli della Toscana Centrale IGT 2016
text:
## Fontodi Flaccianello della Pieve Colli della Toscana Centrale IGT 2016

**The story.** Fontodi is in [Panzano](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Fontodi,+Panzano+in+Chianti,+Italy&t=k), a hill village in the commune of [Greve in Chianti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greve_in_Chianti), in the heart of the [Chianti Classico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chianti) zone between [Florence](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Florence,+Italy&t=k) and [Siena](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Siena,+Italy&t=k). The Manetti family bought the estate in 1968 ([Superiore.de](https://www.superiore.de/en/wine/tuscany-chianti/fontodi/flaccianello-della-pieve-colli-toscana-centrale-igt-2021-bio.html)). The family is also famous for something else: they are still leading makers of Tuscan [terracotta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terracotta), and the German merchant Superiore.de opens its Fontodi profile by asking what the dome of [Florence Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florence_Cathedral) and some of Tuscany's best red wines have in common: the Manetti family. While his older brother Marco looks after the terracotta tradition, Giovanni Manetti has led Fontodi since his youth; he started helping at 16 and planted his first vines in the vineyards below Panzano. Today the estate has about 80 hectares of certified [organic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organic_farming) vines and makes about 400,000 bottles a year, with Franco and Marco Bernabei as oenologists ([Superiore.de](https://www.superiore.de/en/wine/tuscany-chianti/fontodi/flaccianello-della-pieve-colli-toscana-centrale-igt-2021-bio.html)). In 2018 Giovanni Manetti was elected president of the Chianti Classico Consortium; Robert Parker's Wine Advocate wrote that he and Fontodi "represent the pinnacle of quality that can be achieved in this part of Tuscany".

**The vineyards: the Conca d'Oro.** Fontodi's vines lie in Panzano's "Conca d'Oro" (golden basin). Antonio Galloni of Vinous writes that all the natural intensity of the Conca d'Oro comes through in Flaccianello ([Fine+Rare](https://www.frw.co.uk/product/612ec280010000000004c185/2016-flaccianello-della-pieve-fontodi)). Since 2001, Flaccianello has been a selection of the best grapes from three plots on the estate, mainly the highest ones at around 480 metres, where a stony sandstone conglomerate called Pietraforte gives the wine its freshness and structure ([Superiore.de](https://www.superiore.de/en/wine/tuscany-chianti/fontodi/flaccianello-della-pieve-colli-toscana-centrale-igt-2021-bio.html)).

**The wine: Flaccianello della Pieve.** In 1981 Giovanni Manetti, just twenty, made the first vintage with Franco Bernabei: a pure [Sangiovese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangiovese), at a time when the rules for Chianti Classico still required some white grapes in the blend. What began as an act of rebellion became a legend, and Flaccianello became one of the first single-variety "Super Tuscans" ([Superiore.de](https://www.superiore.de/en/wine/tuscany-chianti/fontodi/flaccianello-della-pieve-colli-toscana-centrale-igt-2021-bio.html)). Because it broke the rules of the day, it is sold as IGT Colli della Toscana Centrale rather than Chianti Classico. The name comes from the original vineyard; "pieve" is the Italian word for an old rural parish church ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pieve)), many of them [Romanesque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanesque_architecture).

For the 2016, the Wine Advocate's Monica Larner reports a change in the cellar: until 2013 Flaccianello spent 24 months in small barrels (barriques); since then, six months of that time is spent in larger casks (botti), and the 2016 included a small part aged in clay [amphorae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amphora) for the first time, which she says made the wine more elegant. Cool weather at flowering cut 2016 yields by 20% compared with 2015, and about 65,000 bottles were made ([JJ Buckley, critics' notes](https://www.jjbuckley.com/wine/2016-fontodi-flaccianello-della-pieve/2016-6539-750/)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [Tuscany vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/tuscany) calls 2016 another good vintage, with deep colour and impressive fragrance, though yields were down by up to a fifth. Chianti Classico had particularly good fruit. Larner describes it as a "balanced vintage" with undisputed quality of fruit.

**What the critics say for 2016.** As listed by [JJ Buckley](https://www.jjbuckley.com/wine/2016-fontodi-flaccianello-della-pieve/2016-6539-750/) and [Fine+Rare](https://www.frw.co.uk/product/612ec280010000000004c185/2016-flaccianello-della-pieve-fontodi):
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 100** (Monica Larner, July 2019). "A masterpiece." Tasted blind next to the 2016 [Masseto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornellaia), she found this "an even more beautiful portrait of a perfect Tuscan landscape", thanks to Sangiovese's tangy character: dark cherry, blue flowers and tilled earth, taut, almost crunchy tannins, and remarkable depth. Drink 2020 to 2050.
- **[Vinous](https://vinous.com): 100** (Antonio Galloni, September 2020). "A truly special, moving wine": beautifully layered, with remarkable finesse and power, showing "the darker side of Sangiovese". Drink 2026 to 2041.
- **Jane Anson: 98** (October 2025). One of the original Super Tuscans, outside the rules not for foreign grapes but for being 100% Sangiovese. Supple, savoury and vivid, with rose, violet, sandalwood, incense and baking spice, and a salty finish. "In a sweet spot for drinking", and relatively great value among Super Tuscans. Drink 2025 to 2040.
- **[Wine Spectator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_Spectator): 97** (Bruce Sanderson, October 2019). Mulberry, plum, black cherry, mineral and spice; lush yet firmly structured, with racy acidity. Best 2021 to 2040; 4,300 cases made.
- **[James Suckling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Suckling): 95** (April 2019). Dark cherries, blackcurrant, bramble, eucalyptus, tar, sandalwood and dried violets; very refined and delicate. Better from 2022.
- **[Wine Enthusiast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_Enthusiast): 94** (Kerin O'Keefe, July 2020). Wild berry, new leather, exotic spice and eucalyptus; [Marasca cherry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marasca_cherry), prune, licorice and tobacco, with firm young tannins. Drink 2026 to 2036.
- **[Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson): 18/20** (Walter Speller, October 2024). Mint over cherry and raspberry; cool sour cherry on the palate, fluid, elegant and long, "liquid elegance of substance". Drink 2024 to 2038.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 94.9** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is ten years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2024 to 2050, Jane Anson tasted it in 2025 and found it in a sweet spot for drinking, and Vinous's window opened this year. So it is entering its prime, with decades ahead. Decant 1 to 2 hours ahead. If you have several bottles, open one now and keep the rest for the 2030s.

**Serving.** Fontodi's merchant suggests serving its Flaccianello at 18 to 20°C ([Superiore.de](https://www.superiore.de/en/wine/tuscany-chianti/fontodi/flaccianello-della-pieve-colli-toscana-centrale-igt-2021-bio.html)); I'd start a little cooler and let it warm in a large glass. Sangiovese's high acidity makes it a wonderful wine with food.

**Food.** Superiore.de suggests a wild boar ragù with braised white beans. My picks for a great Tuscan red: [bistecca alla fiorentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bistecca_alla_fiorentina), [pappardelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pappardelle) with [wild boar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_boar) ragù, [pici](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pici) with a meat sauce, roast lamb with rosemary, or an aged [pecorino toscano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pecorino_toscano). I'd avoid very spicy dishes.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the three stores on this site lists Flaccianello at the moment. Fine-wine merchants such as [JJ Buckley](https://www.jjbuckley.com/wine/2016-fontodi-flaccianello-della-pieve/2016-6539-750/) and [Fine+Rare](https://www.frw.co.uk/product/612ec280010000000004c185/2016-flaccianello-della-pieve-fontodi) carry it, and in Germany Superiore.de lists the current 2022 at €116 a bottle. For a 100-point wine, Jane Anson's "relatively great value" is fair.

**From the history books**
- **Chianti's first borders, 1716.** In 1716 [Cosimo III de' Medici](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosimo_III_de'_Medici), Grand Duke of Tuscany, issued an edict naming the villages of the Lega del Chianti ([Castellina](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Castellina+in+Chianti,+Italy&t=k), [Gaiole](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Gaiole+in+Chianti,+Italy&t=k) and [Radda](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Radda+in+Chianti,+Italy&t=k)), plus [Greve](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Greve+in+Chianti,+Italy&t=k) and a stretch of hillside nearby, as the only official producers of Chianti, one of the first legal wine boundaries in the world ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chianti)).
- **Ricasoli's recipe.** In the 19th century Baron [Bettino Ricasoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bettino_Ricasoli), later Prime Minister of Italy, made Sangiovese the backbone of Chianti; over time the recipe came to include white grapes such as Malvasia ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chianti)).
- **The Super Tuscan rebellion.** In the 1970s, ambitious producers frustrated by old-fashioned rules, which forced them to blend in white grapes, began making wines outside the official system: some pure Sangiovese like Flaccianello, others with [Cabernet Sauvignon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabernet_Sauvignon) or [Merlot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merlot). Their prices and scores often outshone official Chianti, and the rules were changed: since 1995 Chianti may be 100% Sangiovese ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chianti)).
- **Greve's new name.** In 1932 the Chianti area was redrawn, and Greve added "in Chianti" to its name in 1972 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chianti)).

**Curious details**
- **The black rooster.** Only Chianti Classico may carry the black rooster (gallo nero) seal on the neck of the bottle, showing the producer is a member of the Chianti Classico Consortium, which Giovanni Manetti went on to lead ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chianti)). Flaccianello, as an IGT, doesn't carry it.
- **The straw flask.** Chianti was long sold in the squat, straw-wrapped "fiasco" bottle, now used by only a few makers ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chianti)).
- **Side by side with Masseto.** In Larner's blind tasting, Flaccianello held its own beside Masseto, the famous Merlot from the [Ornellaia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornellaia) estate ([JJ Buckley](https://www.jjbuckley.com/wine/2016-fontodi-flaccianello-della-pieve/2016-6539-750/)).
- **Ancient vines from Lamole.** For his vineyards, Manetti took cuttings from old bush-trained Sangiovese vines from the 1920s that survived in the high village of [Lamole](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Lamole,+Greve+in+Chianti,+Italy&t=k), at 620 metres ([Superiore.de](https://www.superiore.de/en/wine/tuscany-chianti/fontodi/flaccianello-della-pieve-colli-toscana-centrale-igt-2021-bio.html)).
